To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The Schottky barrier of a nanowire depends on the wire diameter, and 2) the diameter dependence is due to electrostatic effects.

the diameter dependence of the Schottky barrier in metal-wrapped cylindrical semiconductor nanowires is much stronger than the image-force lowering effect, and that this is due to the reduced depletion charge in thin nanowires, which reduces the potential drop on interfacial layers.

the diameter dependence of the Schottky barrier is stronger in thin nanowires compared to thicker ones, and that this is a consequence of the interplay between the electrostatic properties and the non-ideal properties of the interface, as well as of the image-force barrier lowering effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diameter dependence of Schottky barriers on metal-wrapped cylindrical semiconductor nanowires.
a new class of Schottky diode, which consists of a cylindrical semiconductor wire wrapped in an ideal metal.
the diameter dependence of the non-ideal (i.e., with interfacial layer) Schottky barrier heights of metal-wrapped cylindrical semiconducting nanowires.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the diameter dependence of the non-ideal barrier height is a significant and unavoidable effect, which should be considered when designing metal-nanowires Schottky diodes, especially when the nanowires are thin.

the diameter dependence of non-ideal Schmitt barrier height is significant, and the effect is expected to be stronger than that of image-force barrier reduction; however, this effect is not expected to be the dominating one in the diameter dependence of the barrier height.
, for the systems studied, the diameter dependence of the non-ideal barrier height is a significant factor that should not be neglected when comparing experimental results with simulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the diameter dependence of the barrier height in metal-nanowires is not negligible, and it can be a significant factor in nanoscale devices, especially in the case of nanowires with diameters below 100 nm.
the non-ideal barrier height in a metal-nanowires system depends on the nanowire radius; the effect can be as strong as O(10−50) meV for nanowires of 10–50 nm in diameter.

the non-ideal nature of metal-semiconductor interfaces is expected to have a strong effect on the Schottky barrier heights of thin metal-wrapped nanosystems, and that this effect is not accounted for in the existing literature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diameter dependence of the Schottky barrier is a significant effect in metal-wrapped nanoelectronic devices.
the diameter dependence of the Schottky barrier should be considered when designing nanoscale metal-semiconductor devices.
metal-semiconductor nanowire systems are not ideal, and that this effect can be significant for thin nanowires.
